text.title: rust-tokio-async Failure Modes
text.summary: 8 failure modes observed when applying the rust-tokio-async methodology. Each pairs symptom + root-cause + concrete fix.

antipattern.symptom: Service calls try_join! over 10K items; runtime allocates 10K tasks and OOMs the pod.
antipattern.fix: Switch to stream::iter(...).buffer_unordered(N) with N tied to backend pool size.

antipattern.symptom: Argon2 hashing inside an async handler stalls all other requests on the same worker.
External HTTP call hangs forever; the worker pool exhausts.
let g = mutex.lock(); some_io.await; deadlocks on multi_thread runtime.
antipattern.fix: Narrow the critical section to before .await, or use tokio::sync::Mutex.

antipattern.symptom: select! between an HTTP read and shutdown drops the read mid-buffer.
antipattern.fix: Document the unsafe branch + structure as a loop with biased select, OR move the read into a JoinSet.

antipattern.symptom: Latency spikes with no obvious cause; a flamegraph shows one worker thread frozen for 200ms inside `std::fs::read`.
antipattern.root-cause: A synchronous filesystem call sits directly inside an async handler.
antipattern.fix: `tokio::task::spawn_blocking(|| std::fs::read(path))`, or switch the call site to `tokio::fs`.

antipattern.symptom: OOMKilled overnight with no traffic anomaly; metrics show 10M messages queued.
antipattern.root-cause: `mpsc::unbounded_channel` in front of a consumer that is slower than the producer.
antipattern.fix: Switch to bounded `mpsc::channel(1024)` sized to measured load; the producer then experiences back-pressure instead of the heap doing so.

antipattern.symptom: Spawned tasks panic silently — the work simply never happens and the logs show nothing at all.
antipattern.root-cause: `tokio::spawn(...)` called without retaining the JoinHandle; the panic is captured into a handle nobody awaits.
antipattern.fix: Use `JoinSet` and await the results; panics propagate through the `Result` returned by `join_next`.
